title.narrative: Sudan - ACJR 2026 (Project & Program incl Joint Budget)

description.narrative: FPDO and Plan worked closely together to design this project as a result of Plan's localisation effort and pre-existing collaboration through the ongoing PCJR. While FPDO will lead procurement and delivery to communal kitchens in Tawila, food basket distribution in Dar-El-Salam, leveraging its pre-existing experience, Plan will manage MPC distribution and protection mainstreaming. HH identification will be carried out jointly between the two organisations in consultations with the community members. FPDO was involved at every stage of this intervention's design, from needs analysis through activity selection and targeting, ensuring the response reflects community priorities and access realities. Plan provides FPDO with technical oversight and capacity building, safeguarding support, financial management, and joint monitoring to ensure delivery against humanitarian standards. The proposed intervention will not only complement but also leverage ongoing PCJR activities in the area, including clear referral pathways to CP activities. Regular coordination with JR agencies will take place to avoid a duplication of effort and ensure the most efficient coverage of IPC 5 areas. Plan has closely coordinated with other JR partners (2b).

Plan and FPDO already delivered a similar design in the PCJR’s CM in the targeted areas, with pre-established procurement channels and contracts, enabling partners to deliver all activities for this ACJR in 9 weeks, timed before the lean season intensifies the ongoing hunger crisis. MPC and FSL activities will be implemented simultaneous. MPC in Tawila’s IDP camps: stakeholder mobilisation, market assessments, and inception (Week 1), HH identification and registration (Weeks 2-4), cash transfers (Weeks 5-6), and post-distribution monitoring (Weeks 8-9). FSL runs simultaneously: communal kitchen setup and food procurement (Week 1), community kitchen operations (Weeks 2-5), and food basket HH registration and distribution in Dar-El-Salam’s IDP camps (Weeks 1-4). This compressed timeline reflects the urgency of IPC 5 conditions, with first MPC and food basket beneficiaries reached by Week 5 and kitchens operational by Week 2.

SUMMARY: The intervention provides combined cash and food assistance to IDPs in Tawila and Dar-El-Salam, tailored to market conditions. In Tawila, 785 vulnerable households receive multipurpose cash, while 520 households access communal kitchens. In Dar-El-Salam, 431 households receive in-kind food baskets due to market disruption. Protection is integrated throughout via helpdesks, referrals, child-focused targeting, and risk awareness sessions. Coordination with partners ensures complementary coverage and referral pathways for mobile IDPs.

The fall of Al Fasher (Oct 2025) displaced 106,000 people to Tawila and Dar-El-Salam, pushing several areas into IPC Phase 5 with extreme food insecurity .
In Tawila, 31,795 people are in IPC 5, and 41,672 more across nearby areas. Most displaced households eat less than one meal per day, with overwhelmed communal kitchens and collapsing market access due to hyperinflation. In Dar-El-Salam, markets are largely non-functional. Around 70% of the displaced are women and children, with severe child malnutrition and high vulnerability among UASCs, elderly, and PwD.
Plan and FPDO, with partners, propose a 9-week emergency FSL and MPC response: cash and Takaya support in Tawila, and direct food distribution in Dar-El-Salam, to prevent famine-level outcomes before the lean season.

The intervention targets areas that are hosting large numbers of IDPs classified as IPC 5. This intervention will prioritise based on needs (IPC 5), ensuring that a minimum of 80% of beneficiaries are IDPs, and 20% host communities also classified as IPC 5. Priority is given to female- and child-headed HH, UASCs, families with malnourished children, PwD, PLW, and women and girls facing heightened GBV risks. HH identification is conducted jointly by Plan and FPDO through ERRs and community feedback mechanisms, ensuring populations in smaller rural IDP sites are not excluded. Inclusion is operationalised through adapted distribution points for PwD and PLW, dedicated food rations for UASCs, protection helpdesks with CP case management referrals, and PSEA and child safeguarding feedback mechanisms at all delivery points.

The project delivers combined MPC and emergency food assistance with integrated protection, adapted to market conditions.
In Tawila, 785 HHs (3,925 people) receive MPC (161 EUR/HH) in two IDP camps, while 520 HHs (2,600 people) receive hot meals via supported communal kitchens (takaya).
In Dar-El-Salam, 431 HHs (2,155 people) receive direct food baskets due to market collapse.
Protection is mainstreamed through helpdesks, referrals to case management, child-focused targeting (including UASCs), and risk awareness sessions, with coordination to ensure coverage of mobile IDPs.
